drugs.moa: Binds opioid receptors in the CNS to relieve moderate-to-severe pain.
nursing: Assess respiratory rate before and after (hold if RR < 12)
Start a bowel regimen to prevent constipation
teaching: Prevent constipation with fluids and fiber
drugs.tip: Opioids: watch RESPIRATORY RATE (hold if <12), cause constipation, antidote = naloxone. Have Narcan ready.
drugs.pearl: **Opioids → respiratory depression + constipation.** Reverse with naloxone.

drugs.moa: Displaces opioids from their receptors, rapidly reversing respiratory depression and sedation.
adverse: Recurrence of respiratory depression as it wears off
nursing: Short duration — the opioid may outlast it, so keep monitoring
teaching: The person must be watched after a dose — it can wear off before the opioid does
drugs.tip: Naloxone reverses opioids but is SHORT-acting — the opioid can outlast it. Keep monitoring; repeat if needed.

drugs.moa: Enhances GABA in the CNS, producing sedation, anti-anxiety, and anticonvulsant effects.
nursing: Monitor respiratory status with IV use
teaching: Avoid alcohol and other CNS depressants
drugs.tip: Benzodiazepines (-lam/-pam): CNS + respiratory depression, antidote = flumazenil. Don't stop abruptly.

drugs.moa: Stabilizes neuronal membranes and limits seizure spread.
nursing: Give IV slowly with normal saline only (precipitates in dextrose)
Meticulous oral care for gum overgrowth
teaching: Brush and floss well; see your dentist regularly
drugs.tip: Phenytoin: level 10–20, gingival hyperplasia (oral care!), IV in NS only & slow, watch for rash (SJS).

drugs.moa: Increases serotonin availability in the brain to improve mood and anxiety.
adverse: Increased suicidal thoughts early in treatment (esp. young adults)
nursing: Monitor mood and suicide risk early on
Don't combine with MAOIs or other serotonergic drugs
teaching: It takes weeks to work — keep taking it
Report worsening mood or thoughts of self-harm
drugs.tip: SSRIs: 2–6 weeks to work, monitor suicide risk early, watch serotonin syndrome, no MAOIs.
drugs.pearl: **Serotonin syndrome:** high fever, agitation, tremor, sweating, hyperreflexia.

drugs.moa: Stabilizes mood; exact mechanism unclear. Narrow therapeutic range.
adverse: Lithium toxicity (coarse tremor, vomiting, confusion, seizures)
nursing: Maintain steady sodium and fluid intake (low sodium/dehydration raises levels)
teaching: Drink plenty of fluids and keep salt intake steady
Report vomiting, diarrhea, coarse tremor, or confusion
drugs.tip: Lithium level 0.6–1.2 (narrow!). Low sodium/dehydration → toxicity. Coarse tremor = toxic; fine tremor = expected.

drugs.moa: Blocks dopamine receptors to reduce psychotic symptoms and agitation.
nursing: Watch for NMS: high fever, rigidity, altered mental status, autonomic instability
teaching: Report muscle stiffness, high fever, or uncontrollable movements
drugs.tip: Antipsychotics: watch EPS and NMS (high fever + rigidity = emergency). Tardive dyskinesia with long-term use.
drugs.pearl: **NMS = Fever + Rigid + Altered mental + Vitals unstable** → stop drug, emergency.
